st.headline: Investment-linked insurance v participating plans: What drives demand and which suits you better
st.teaser: Interest stems from rising costs, longer lives and a need for discipline.
fullText: SINGAPORE – After spending nearly a decade selling investment-linked insurance policies (ILPs) – hybrid products that combine investing with insurance coverage – former financial adviser Bobby Sim said the experience was “one of the reasons why I could not stay in the industry”.
Sim, who worked at Manulife and later advisory firm Finexis, shared that high commissions, particularly in the first two years, heavily incentivised insurance agents to push ILPs.
“Most of us sold what the company recommended, without fully understanding the returns behind the product,” he said.
“I am not saying every agent is bad. But if you look at net returns after fees, most of the ILPs I saw did worse than simply putting the money into the S&P 500.”
That experience shaped his personal financial planning – he now keeps his investments separate from his family’s insurance protection needs.
“When you mix the two in one product, you usually get a worse version of both,” he noted.

That said, Sim feels that ILPs may still suit three types of buyers: those who lack the discipline not to spend their money; those with an agent who consistently beats the market after fees; and those who lack the bandwidth to manage their own finances and prefer leaving both insurance and investments to a trusted adviser.

Latest figures from the Life Insurance Association Singapore (LIA) show that new life insurance sales from ILPs – measured by weighted new business premiums – rose 22.6% year on year to $2.51 billion in the first nine months of 2026.
These plans made up 46% of all new sales, up from 43% over the same period in 2025 and 37% in 2024.
P articipating (par) life insurance policies also recorded growth, with weighted new sales rising 5.7% to $1.24 billion over the same nine-month period.
Par plans accounted for 23% of all new sales in the first nine months of 2026, down slightly from 25% in 2024 and 2025.
These plans fall into three categories: whole life insurance, endowment savings plans and retirement income plans.

Rachel Luo, senior director of sales at Manulife Advisory Group, said interest in ILPs and par plans is driven by greater awareness of long-term financial planning, concerns about rising costs and longevity, and a desire for structure and discipline.
She added that many consumers lack the time, knowledge and confidence to manage a portfolio actively.
While both types of policies have investment components, they work differently, and the choice between an ILP and a par plan ultimately comes down to how much risk a consumer can bear.
Helen Shen, group head of products at Singlife, said ILPs bundle insurance protection with market exposure through investment sub-funds.
A policy’s value depends on the performance of the funds, minus insurance coverage and other fees.
Returns fluctuate with the market, and policyholders bear all the investment risk.
These products therefore suit customers who are comfortable riding out market cycles for potentially higher returns and want more flexibility to choose their own funds, Shen noted.

Manulife’s Luo sees interest in ILPs among younger and mid-career working adults, noting that these clients have longer investment horizons and are just starting to build their wealth and protection portfolios.
Unlike ILPs, which have no guaranteed cash value, par plans have a portion that is guaranteed.
Policyholders pay premiums that go into the insurer’s participating fund.
They share in the fund’s profits and receive a combination of guaranteed benefits and non-guaranteed bonuses.
The guaranteed portion – known as the guaranteed surrender value – is smaller if they cash out early, while the full guaranteed benefit is paid if they hold to maturity.
In exchange for that stability, policyholders have no say in asset selection – the insurer decides how the money is invested across a portfolio of assets.
Shen noted that the “sweet spot” for par plans lies in balancing guaranteed benefits with non-guaranteed bonuses to boost total returns.
She added that this balance suits customers who are cautious about market volatility and want stability without giving up growth potential.
These customers are typically more focused on protecting and managing their wealth over the longer term, Shen said.
Luo pointed out that young families may buy whole life par plans to safeguard against the loss of a breadwinner’s income due to death, total and permanent disability or critical illness.
Separately, endowment par policies are commonly used to fund children’s future education.

cna.headline: China says reserves right to take 'measures' after new US tariffs
cna.teaser: China says reserves right to take 'measures' after new US tariffs
fullText: BEIJING: China said on Thursday (Nov 26) it reserves the right to take "necessary measures" after Washington unveiled new tariffs that could shake the uneasy truce in the two economic giants' trade war.
Chinese commerce ministry spokesman He Yadong told a regular briefing that citing "overcapacity" as a reason to impose tariffs was a "pretext for protectionism".

"Such actions not only fail to address their own structural imbalances but also disrupt the security and stability of global industrial and supply chains, hinder industrial cooperation, drive up global inflation, harm the direct interests of businesses and consumers and pose long-term, systemic risks to global economic growth," He said.
"China urges the United States to correct its erroneous practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation," He added.
US President Donald Trump has long criticised China's yawning trade surplus with the United States, which he has blamed for a decline in local manufacturing prowess and jobs.
After starting a second term in office last year, Trump imposed new tariffs on Chinese goods, kicking off a tit-for-tat escalation that at one point saw duties touch 145 per cent.
The trade ceasefire struck by Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in October 2025 is due to expire in January, after a two-month extension was agreed in September.
Th two men met last week at an APEC summit in Shenzhen in southern China and are due to see each other for the fourth time this year in December at a G20 summit in the United States.
The proposed new US levies target a range of trading partners including China, the European Union and Japan and range up to 20 per cent.
China is among those facing the highest 20-per cent rate, but US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the new levies were within the bounds of existing trade negotiations with Beijing.

"China understands that we're going to have some level of tariffs. This falls within that understanding," he told US broadcaster CNBC, adding that the US was offering China exemptions on around US$30 billion of goods.

economistArticle.title: The Hidden Costs of Mandated Affordability
paras: Political leaders worldwide are increasingly obsessed with a single word: affordability. Facing voter fury over rising living costs, governments from Washington to European capitals are rushing to promise subsidised housing, capped utility prices, and discounted childcare. Yet beneath these populist promises lies a sobering economic paradox—attempting to make life artificially cheap often ends up costing the public purse far more than expected.

When fiscal policy attempts to suppress market prices without addressing supply constraints, the results are predictably counterproductive. Subsidies inevitably stimulate demand while failing to incentivize producers to expand output. In the housing sector, for example, mortgage assistance programs meant to help first-time buyers frequently drive up home prices even further, neutralizing the initial policy objective and expanding public debt.

Furthermore, interventionist price controls distort price signals that are vital for efficient capital allocation. When energy tariffs are capped below market clearing levels, energy companies curtail capital expenditure on next-generation infrastructure. The resulting underinvestment compromises long-term energy security, creating a fiscal burden that future taxpayers must eventually shoulder.

The fiscal math is growing precarious. As sovereign debt burdens soar in major advanced economies, continuous interventions to subsidise consumption strain already overstretched state budgets. Sovereign bond yields rise when financial markets begin to doubt a government's long-term spending discipline, driving up borrowing costs across the entire real economy.

True affordability cannot be engineered through decree or continuous subsidies. Policymakers must focus on productivity growth, deregulation, and structural reforms that lower the actual cost of production. Until governments accept that genuine affordability requires expanding supply rather than masking costs, their economic relief measures will remain an expensive illusion.
economistArticle.cn:
世界各地的政治领导人越来越执着于一个词：住房与生活成本的“可负担性”。面对选民对生活成本上涨的愤怒，从华盛顿到欧洲各国的政府都在争先恐后地承诺住房补贴、限制公用事业价格以及打折托儿服务。然而，在这些民粹主义承诺的背后，隐藏着一个令人深思的经济悖论——试图人为地让生活变得便宜，最终往往会让公共财政付出一比预期大得多的代价。
当财政政策试图在不解决供给约束的情况下压制市场价格时，其结果必然适得其反。补贴不可避免地刺激了需求，却无法激励生产商扩大产出。例如，在住房领域，旨在帮助首次购房者的房贷补贴计划往往会进一步推高房价，从而抵消了最初的政策目标，并扩大了公共债务。
此外，干预性的价格管制扭曲了对高效资本配置至关重要的价格信号。当能源资费被限制在市场结清水平以下时，能源公司就会削减对下一代基础设施的资本支出。由此导致的投资不足损害了长期能源安全，创造了未来纳税人最终必须承担的财政负担。
财政账本正变得日益危险。随着主要发达经济体的主权债务负担飙升，补贴消费的持续干预使本已过度紧张的国家预算雪上加霜。当金融市场开始怀疑政府的长期支出纪律时，主权债券收益率就会上升，从而推高整个实体经济的借贷成本。
真正的“可负担性”无法通过法令或持续补贴来工程化地制造出来。政策制定者必须专注于生产力增长、去监管化以及降低实际生产成本的结构性改革。在政府承认真正的可负担性需要扩大供给而非掩盖成本之前，其经济缓解措施将始终是一种昂贵的幻觉。

gems.s: Subsidies inevitably stimulate demand while failing to incentivize producers to expand output.
gems.why: Uses a contrasting sentence structure ('while failing to...') to clearly highlight the asymmetry between demand generation and supply response in economic policy. 使用对比句式（“while failing to...”）清晰地凸显了经济政策中需求刺激与供给响应之间的不对称性。

gems.s: Until governments accept that genuine affordability requires expanding supply rather than masking costs, their economic relief measures will remain an expensive illusion.
gems.why: Employs a persuasive conditional opening frame ('Until...') paired with sharp antithesis ('expanding supply rather than masking costs') to deliver a strong concluding synthesis. 采用具说服力的条件句作为开头框架（“Until...”），结合鲜明的对照手法（“expanding supply rather than masking costs”），给出了强有力的总结性结论。
